'Never handed over' before a packet existed; 'Outcome sign-off outstanding' with only the code approved ('The code review is signed off by Default Admin. The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding.'); 'Changes requested' after I handed the criteria list back; 'Sign-offs are stale' once the tree moved past the packet ('any sign-off on record is about a different change'). In all four the 'Push to an OCI repository' and 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' rows render with no checkbox at all - `[data-testid=barn-publish-target-oci]` and `-repository` matched 0 - so they cannot be committed, and the submit stayed disabled at 'Pick a destination'. What I could not show is the positive half (the same publish then proceeding), because the OCI push is not built and the repository route needs a GitHub token this Studio has no way to obtain; both rows say so in their own words rather than pretending.

Created an extension from screen 02 (description, outcome, name 'w6bvc', placement 'Inside a cluster'). Re-drove all five against the installed bundle, because this round changed the hand-over path, the publish summary, the masthead and the shared scanners. CLI: 'Show raw output' [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] expands in one click and renders the pod's real log - I read 'DONE Compiled successfully in 3457ms', 'App running at: - Local: http://localhost:8005' and a later 'WAIT Compiling...1:58:41 AM' out of it, with timestamps that match the pod's actual dev server, and the panel says 'the terminal is still here'. The Terminal tab attaches a live xterm (canvas present) to the pod's tmux session, and I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` five separate times during this run. FILES: /barn/extensions/base/files lists the tree with branches and last-commit information and opens a file. GITHUB IMPORT: the Import dialog does connection as step 1 inline ('you can paste it here without losing what you have typed'), with no link out to settings. PUBLISH: the dialog renders all five destinations with their gates. SETTINGS: /barn/settings renders connection, the sign-off matrix, permissions, access and data. The masthead change did not cost anything - the editor gear that used to open a second token modal is gone and nothing else went with it; the raw-output button and the Terminal tab are both still one click from the assistant panel.

Both routes, both landing in the same place, both with the reviewer's own wording. From a hunk on screen 12: opened the composer on line 1, typed 'W6BVC cross probe: rename this probe file before merging.' and pressed 'Send to the assistant' - the pod's tmux pane then held 'A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about verify-w6bvc-scope.ts around line 1. Their words: W6BVC cross probe: rename this probe file before merging.. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' From the decision bar: 'Request changes' opened a modal that says what it does ('recorded against the code review... also put straight to the assistant working in base's pod, so the change is made by the thing that wrote it rather than by you'), and sending it recorded changes-requested in the review record and routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the terminal attached and the paragraph already in the session. The reviewer writes a sentence, never a fix, and the author still has to act on it.

Screen 12 measures from the last published version and says so out loud. With one uncommitted file in base the header read 'Reviewing all 1 file' and the narrowing sentence read 'Showing what has landed since <sha>, the commit you last read... The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 1 file. Approve still commits all of it.' The intermediate history is not shown: I made three commits into base during this run (two hand-over sweeps and a review commit) and the review screen never listed them as steps - it showed the net difference only. Screen 04 says the same thing about the same baseline ('Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree.').

Judged as two halves, because they now behave differently. CONNECTION: passes. Screen 03's strip [data-testid=barn-session-state] reads 'The assistant is not signed in . run /login in the terminal', and screen 09's [data-testid=settings-assistant-login] reads 'The assistant is not signed in', with the detail row naming every pod it asked ('No credential in any of these pods (base, demo, nodehealth, v6r)... and the workspace's own session strip says the same'). Both come from the same `assistantLogin()` reading of the pod, so they are one state in two places. The GitHub side agrees too: settings names the account ('Not connected'), and the editor masthead's gear that used to open a second bare token modal no longer exists - `grep -rn barn-editor-settings-button --include=*.vue` finds only a comment. The remaining EditorSettingsModal openings are inline in flows with something in flight (the create form, the import dialog, the hand-over), which is what the design's own rationale row asks for, and they write through the same connectGithub into the same Secret. PERMISSION: still fails, and the product now says why rather than hiding it.
verdicts.defect: The permission mode is not one state in two places and cannot be. Screen 03's chip reports the live session ('Planning only, no edits'); screen 09 reports the mode the pod starts in ('Edits apply without asking'), and marks the radio group not settable. The two disagreed on screen while I looked at them. What changed this round is that neither screen pretends otherwise: [data-testid=barn-permission-split] on screen 03 spells the divergence out ('Two readings of two different things, and neither screen can change the other'), and [data-testid=settings-permission-fixed] explains that the pod starts claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions from a ConfigMap the bundle rewrites on every page load, so a level chosen on the page would be undone within seconds. Honest, but the rule asks for one state settable in one place, and that is not what exists.

verdicts.evidence: Authored once, walked once, on an extension I created for the purpose so nothing else could account for it. Wrote 'W6BVC MARKER: the trend panel names the window it covers' into the first acceptance criterion on screen 10 for w6bvc; the page saved it ('Saved 02:18 AM') and BRIEF.md in that pod gained '- [ ] W6BVC MARKER: the trend panel names the window it covers' under '## How we will know it worked'. Screen 13 for the same extension then listed exactly that one criterion, with Yes / No / Can't tell / Show me against it, and nothing was re-entered anywhere. I then exercised it against the running build: 'Show me' drove the pinned preview (that pod's own dev server through the apiserver proxy) to /home and 'Capture this as evidence' wrote '- Captured 2026-08-24 02:19 by Default Admin at `/home`' into the file under that criterion. So the criterion, the walk and the evidence are one chain through three screens.

Inspected the rendered markup of the Studio screens again. The Studio is built from its own S-prefixed primitives in pkg/barn/components/ui (SButton, SChip, SBanner, SCard, STabs, SMenu, SModal, SField). On screen 01, document.querySelectorAll('.sortable-table') is 0, and the table is a div grid: .studio-home__table with hand-rolled .studio-home__th headers (State, Name, Source, Running on, Last change). None of Rancher's own component classes appear either - .labeled-input 0, .banner 0, .async-button 0, .tabbed 0.
verdicts.defect: Screen 01 is a bespoke table, not the SortableTable pattern the rationale row names ('the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page'), so the claim that a Rancher user already knows how to read it does not hold. The wider claim is met in spirit (nothing needs a new primitive) but not in fact (the primitives are new implementations of existing ones). Recorded as a deliberate departure in DEPARTURES.md section 1, with the cost it has already had.

verdicts.evidence: Seeded a recorded failure and opened screen 08. It named the cause in words, was honest that it had pattern-matched the log rather than understood it, and offered 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue' and, for the way back, 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 0217 on Aug 24"' taken three minutes earlier, with 'Undo the last change' beside it and '0 changed files since'. The snapshots are real: refs/tags/barn-snap/* in base's pod holds dozens of automatic ones. The screen is also honest about the limit of the guarantee ('A snapshot is a point somebody chose, not necessarily a build that worked') and says rolling back snapshots the failed tree first so nothing is lost.

Everything I did before the publish dialog asked nobody, across four extensions and roughly two hours. Created an extension from screen 02, drafted and edited its brief, agreed one brief and skipped another, added and answered questions, planted and edited files in a pod, ran the scope checks, commented on a hunk and sent it to the assistant, requested changes, opened the failure screen and read its rollback offer, walked verification and signed it off. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control appeared at any point. The only gate chips in the product are on the two distribution rows of the publish dialog; 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' are both chipped 'No sign-off', and settings' [data-testid=settings-iteration-note] says the same in policy terms.

The publish dialog names exactly one hard gate and puts it at the distribution boundary: 'Push to an OCI repository. The gate. The one hard gate in the design: the point an extension becomes installable by people who did not build it, and the only step that asks anybody for permission.' 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' is tagged 'The gate' as the same boundary by the route this Studio can take. Beside them 'Load into this Rancher' is chipped 'No sign-off' and reversible, and 'Push the source to GitHub' is chipped 'No sign-off' because it is how you ask for a review rather than how you leave the gate. Nothing earlier in the walk (01, 02, 10, 03, 04) asked for an approval. The OCI push itself is not built and the row says so plainly rather than drawing a button that lies.

Re-judged against the rule's wording, and the hand-over half has genuinely changed: it no longer needs GitHub and I took it end to end for the first time. From base's publish dialog I ticked 'Push the source to GitHub'; the confirm step said what it would do without a token ('the packet and its branch are written in the pod, the review record gets the entry, and the change appears in the review queue for somebody to sign. No pull request will record it, and the packet will say that rather than imply one exists.'), and pressing 'Hand over' produced packet 2 for real - refs/barn/packets/2 and branch barn/base/2 in the pod, a git note carrying the provenance, an entry in the barn-review-base record, and a queue row on screen 11. The reading half is right too: screen 12's chip reads 'No PR for packet 2' out of the record rather than searching GitHub. But the record the rule names is a PR, and no PR exists.
verdicts.defect: Crossing the gate does not produce a PR in this environment. The packet carries pr: null and pushError 'No GitHub token is configured in this Studio, so the packet was not pushed and no pull request records this hand-over', and the publish status strip repeats it ('packet 2 on barn/base/2, in this cluster only'). The other route across the boundary, 'Push to an OCI repository', is 'Not built' by the dialog's own admission. So what carries the hand-off record here is the packet plus the review record inside the cluster, which is a defensible substitute but is not the flow map's 'the PR is the record'; the product would need a GitHub credential Studio has no way to obtain by itself ('There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own').

verdicts.evidence: base had a dirty working tree and a live preview throughout this run and none of it reached anybody: `kubectl get uiplugins -A` lists only barn and nodehealth, and base's row on screen 01 offers 'Remove the local install' greyed out with the reason 'not installed'. Screen 04 says the same in words: 'Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree. Publishing builds from it; discarding puts it back to the last commit.' Publishing is a separate deliberate act in a dialog where every destination is unticked and the submit reads 'Pick a destination' until you choose one. Snapshots are taken per build - refs/tags/barn-snap/* in the pod, the newest three minutes old when screen 08 offered it.

The brief half passes and the change-level prompt half now passes; the per-hunk half cannot be exercised here. Brief: I wrote a criterion on screen 10 and read it back on 12 and 13, and the packet's own note records whether a BRIEF.md was in the tree at the hand-over. Prompts: they are captured while the author works and they survive into review - screen 12 rendered 'Prompt 1 of 3 / Read BRIEF.md in this package... 15 minutes ago . from the workspace screen' for the prompts gathered behind packet 2, and the packet record carries turns: 3 with the window it counted over.
verdicts.defect: Per hunk is the part that cannot be shown. Screen 12 reports 'No prompt recorded for any of this change's 1 line', and each prompt is annotated 'ended in no commit, so no line can be traced to it'. The reason is the environment: claude in every pod in this cluster answers 'Not logged in . Please run /login' (screen 09 confirms 'No credential in any of these pods'), so no turn ever ends and nothing commits a turn id for the line-level index to blame against. The product says exactly this in [data-testid=barn-stream-stalled] on screen 03. Authoring a change with two distinguishable prompts is not possible until a pod has a credential.

verdicts.evidence: Opened the row menu on /barn/extensions. nodehealth, which is installed as a UIPlugin (cattle-ui-plugin-system/nodehealth v0.1.0), offers an enabled 'Remove the local install v0.1.0' alongside 'Open in the workspace', 'Review changes', 'Open files' and 'Open the brief'. base and the others, which are not installed, show the same item with the reason on it. So the list is where a live extension is taken back, and the item states its own applicability rather than being hidden.

Both amber routes end in the same workspace, and I drove both. Rejection: 'Request changes' on screen 12 routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the xterm attached and the reviewer's paragraph already in the session, not to a remediation screen. Build failure: screen 08's actions are all workspace actions ('Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Undo the last change', 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 0217 on Aug 24"', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue'), and its copy is about returning the same tree rather than branching out of the product. Screen 13's two send-back actions do the same thing by prompt: both put their text into the same pod session. Neither route left the Studio.

Both halves now hold, and the accumulation is a reading rather than a claim. While I worked in base without publishing, the assistant panel on screen 03 carried [data-testid=barn-review-accumulation] and the publish dialog carried the same sentence with numbers in it: 'Since packet 1 was handed over, 0 commits, 1 file, 2 recorded prompts have accumulated in the pod. None of it is in anybody's review queue: it is assembled into packet 2 and handed over at the push, and not before.' Nothing appeared in the review queue during any of that - screen 11 lists only handed-over extensions and says so in its empty state. Pressing the hand-over then assembled it in one go: packet 2 was written with turns: 2 and the window turnsSince it counted over, and screen 12 read it back as '3 prompts were gathered behind packet 3 since 2026-08-24T01:17:09.000Z. The pod still holds exactly what packet N was assembled from, so the diff below and the packet are the same change.' I repeated the cycle for packet 3 and the counts moved with the work. One defect found on the way, worth recording even though it does not break the rule: assemblePacket's `git update-ref refs/barn/packets/<n>` is `;`-chained ahead of `echo BARN-PACKET-OK` and carries no `2>&1`, so when that refs directory was root-owned (left that way by an earlier verifier's root-level git command) the ref write failed with 'Permission denied', the failure was swallowed, and the hand-over reported success while writing a record naming a ref that did not exist. I chowned the directory back to uid 1000 and the same hand-over then wrote the ref correctly. The other write in that chain uses `2>&1`; this one does not.

Planted a file in base's pod whose added line mentions three of the terms the brief's '## What we are deliberately not doing' uses ('alerting', 'history', 'beyond'). Screen 13's Scope card flagged it automatically, named the file per term, and offered both resolutions as real buttons. 'Remove it' put the behaviour to the assistant in the pod with the coincidence caveat and left BRIEF.md byte-identical. 'That is fine - add it to the brief' opened a plan showing exactly what would move, and confirming it rewrote BRIEF.md so the sentence left the non-goals and arrived under 'What changes for them' stamped '(accepted during verification on 2026-08-24 by admin)', with the rest of the sentence left ruled out; the warning then cleared for those terms. [data-testid=verify-scope-limit] is candid that this is a word match over added lines and not a reading of the change.

Per-reviewer state persists and both screens use it. Opening screen 12 recorded a look under my principal in the barn-review-base record ('looks': {pa5g3hz: {principal: local://user-btc48, packet, sha, at}}), which survived reloads and navigations. The queue row then carried the banner with the count: '2 commits and 1 uncommitted file since Default Admin approved this on 2026-08-24. Show only what changed since then', and the demo row carried its own ('6 uncommitted files since...'). On screen 12 [data-testid=rc-since-last-look] narrows the diff and states the relationship to the whole: 'Showing what has landed since <sha>, the commit you last read... The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 1 file. Approve still commits all of it.'

The two records are separate objects with their own verdict, principal, name, timestamp and commit, and neither implies the other. Approving the code on screen 12 wrote signoffs.code and left the outcome row on screen 13 reading 'Outcome sign-off - you - in progress'; signing off the outcome later wrote a second entry with its own timestamp. Handing the criteria list back wrote outcome = changes-requested while code stayed approved, and requesting changes from the code review's decision bar wrote code = changes-requested while the outcome stayed approved - four combinations, all held independently. The roles are separated on the surfaces too: screen 13 tells the reviewer 'You are checking whether this does the job, not whether the code is any good. Reading the code is a separate step, on the review screen, and not this one', and the publish dialog labels the two 'Is it safe?' and 'Does it do the job?'. I could not reproduce the 'Needs a second signer' refusal this round because approving on screen 12 commits the working tree, which moves HEAD past the packet and makes both sign-offs stale before the dialog can compare their principals; the same-signer refusal was observed directly in the previous wave and the code path (`same-signer` in gateFrom/GATE_CHIPS) is unchanged.
